title: G. Isaac's Queries
statement:
You have reached the final level of the popular roguelike game "Isaac's Keybindings". Instead of a boss, you encounter a shopkeeper who holds an hidden array of integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n, where 0 ≤ a_i < 2^30 for each i in [1, n].

It is guaranteed that the array is generated randomly, i.e., each a_i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) is an integer independently generated uniformly at random in [0, 2^30), in all the tests excluding the example.

Let f(u, v) = a_u oplus a_{u+1} oplus … oplus a_v, where oplus is the bitwise textttXOR.

You can ask queries of the following form: texttt? u v, with 1 ≤ u ≤ v ≤ n.

The answer to the query is:

Each query has a cost of 1/(v-u+1) robocoins. On each test, you are given 300 robocoins in total to pass at most 30 test cases (that is, you can spend 10 robocoins on average for a single test case). If your balance ever becomes negative you lose. Note that your robocoin balance does not need to be an integer at any moment.

Find the answer to all possible (n(n+1))/2 queries without losing.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 30). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains one integer n (n = 3 or n = 100) — the length of the array a_1, a_2, …, a_n. It is guaranteed that the array is generated randomly in all the tests excluding the example.

There are exactly 50 tests in this problem (including the example). The example has t = 1 and n = 3, and all the other tests have t = 30 and n = 100.

Hacks are not allowed in this problem.

For each test case, first read a single integer n. If the integer you read is -2, it means that the answer to the previous test case was wrong, and you should exit immediately.

To ask a query, print a line in the format texttt? u v with 1 ≤ u ≤ v ≤ n.

As a response to the query, you will receive -2 if you made an invalid query (i.e., the format is invalid, or you would reach a negative amount of robocoins). In that case, you should exit immediately. Otherwise, you will receive the answer to the query.

When you determine the answers to all the (n(n+1))/2 queries, print them in the following format.

Print n+1 lines. The first line must contain a single character texttt!. The i-th of the next n lines must contain n-i+1 integers: the answers to queries texttt? i i, , texttt? i i+1, ,…, , texttt? i n, respectively.

After printing a query, do not forget to output the end of line and flush the output. Otherwise, you will get textttIdleness limit exceeded. To do this, use:

In the example, the hidden array is [a_1, a_2, a_3] = [2, 4, 6].

Now, even without knowing the hidden array, you claim the answer to all the possible 6 queries. For example, you claim that the answer to texttt? 1 1 is 1.

You have spent 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/2 = 4/3 robocoins, which is less than the allowed 300 robocoins.

Input:
```
1
3

2

-1

1
```

Output:
```
? 1 2

? 1 3

? 2 3

!
1 2 -1 
2 1 
2 
```
